analyst_view.overall: Early view: Sabadell, who like to dominate the ball (66 per cent and 25 shots at Albacete), host a Granada side that has won five league games in a row with efficient, low-possession football. Granada's postponed game with Tenerife still has to be rescheduled, and Óscar Sanz should be back for Sabadell after his ban. Both teams play in round 14 first, so this view will move.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and I agree with a low total. Granada have three clean sheets in their last five league games and Sabadell average about a goal a game at both ends. Sabadell holding the ball against a Granada side happy to wait suggests a slow, low-scoring game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. I lean higher: Sabadell's habit of keeping the ball and shooting often (25 attempts at Albacete) should earn more corners than their 5.1, and Granada were content to let Eldense have the ball and the pressure that came with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards, with 3.2 for Sabadell. I lean lower: the side with most of the ball usually commits fewer fouls, and Sabadell will be that side. Granada may pick up a few for slowing the game, but a total near five looks more likely.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots, with 17.1 for Sabadell, which matches their style. Granada were outshot 13-8 in their last game and still won, so 9.5 for them is fair. I see no reason to move the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.9 shots on target and I leave it. Sabadell's volume comes with modest accuracy, and Granada take few but clean chances (Alcaraz's header and Owen Emeka's late finish at Elda). Worth revisiting after both sides' round-14 games.
